title: Keywords and titles for AI stock images
subtitle: Learn how to write descriptive titles and effective keywords to help buyers find your AI-generated photographs and illustrations.
products: AI image prompt pack for stock sites
html:
Uploading AI-generated art to stock libraries requires a strategic approach to metadata. Without accurate titles and keywords, your files remain invisible to potential buyers searching for specific visual assets.

Mastering this process involves balancing technical descriptions with search terms that reflect buyer intent. This guide covers practical steps to write clear titles, select relevant tags, and avoid common metadata mistakes.

Write clear and factual titles

Stock agency search engines prioritize titles that describe the literal contents of the image. Avoid adding vague adjectives or promotional terms that do not reflect what is actually visible in the frame.

Instead of writing artistic titles, focus on the subject, setting, action, and lighting. For example, use 'Business team collaborating around a wooden table in a modern office' rather than 'Teamwork success'.

Select relevant and specific keywords

Keywords form the backbone of stock photography discoverability. Aim for a mix of broad category tags and narrow, specific descriptors that precisely match the details of your generated asset.

Include elements such as subject matter, color palette, mood, composition, and potential use cases. If your image shows a lone hiker on a foggy mountain trail, include tags like hiking, fog, mountain, solitude, outdoor, and adventure.

Order keywords by importance

Most stock platform algorithms weigh the first few keywords more heavily than the ones placed at the end of the list. Always place the primary subject and core concept at the very beginning of your tag sequence.

Follow the primary subject with secondary details, background elements, and broader conceptual terms. This hierarchy ensures that the search engine indexes the most relevant aspects of the image first.

Avoid common keyword mistakes

A frequent error in metadata tagging is keyword stuffing, which involves adding popular terms that have no relation to the image. Stock platforms routinely penalize accounts that use irrelevant tags to manipulate search results.

Another mistake is omitting technical descriptors. Always include terms that indicate whether the asset is a photograph, a vector illustration, a 3D render, or a digital painting to help buyers filter their searches effectively.

Optimizing your AI stock imagery relies on consistent and accurate description habits. Taking a few extra minutes to refine your titles and tags ensures your work appears in front of the right audience.

Review a batch of your current uploads today and revise their metadata using factual descriptions and prioritized keywords to improve their overall visibility.
